name: Web server
description: A web server on the internet beyond the bench's routers, as a board's HTTP client finds it: its DNS name resolves (through a router's DNS forwarder) to its public address, a TCP connection to its port is accepted, and a GET of its path is answered with its content, then the connection closed. It reaches the circuit only through a router's WAN side (emblink/wifi_ap), the latency it is set at away.

name.doc: Its DNS name; empty for an address alone

port.doc: The TCP port it listens on

latency.doc: Its link's one-way delay to the internet's core

path.doc: The path it serves (a directory's index.html too); any other is 404 Not Found

body.default:
Example Domain

This domain is for use in documentation examples.

outputs.name: log
outputs.doc: Each request: its method, target and version, the client's public address and port, its Host header and the status answered

functional.claims: TCP as a server (RFC 9293): SYN answered by SYN-ACK with an MSS of 1460 and a window of 65535; the client's MSS option (536 without one) and window followed; the request taken in order and acknowledged, a segment out of order answered with the sequence number expected; the response in segments of the MSS within the window, PSH on the last, then FIN; the client's FIN acknowledged; unacknowledged data, SYN-ACK or FIN sent again after 1 s, the time doubling, five times before the connection is reset; TIME-WAIT for 2 s; RST to a segment for no connection. HTTP/1.0 and 1.1 (RFC 9112): GET and HEAD of its path (and of its index.html when it is a directory) answered 200 OK with its Content-Type, Content-Length and Connection: close, an absolute-form target of its path too; another path 404 Not Found, another method 501 Not Implemented, a malformed request 400 Bad Request; the connection closed after the response. ICMP echo requests answered. Reached by its name through a router's DNS forwarder and at its address through the router's NAT (engine/inet.h), its latency on each way. ESP-IDF's protocols/http_request fetches its page unmodified.
omissions: request bodies beyond 2 KB, chunked transfer
more than 8 connections at a time (a SYN beyond them is ignored, as a full backlog does)
the time a server takes to answer (it answers at once)

electrical.claims: As functional: it has no pins.

sources.title: RFC 9293: Transmission Control Protocol
sources.notes: The connection states, the handshake, sequence numbers and acknowledgement, the MSS option, retransmission, RST for segments of no connection.

sources.title: RFC 9112: HTTP/1.1
sources.notes: The request line, the status line, Content-Length and Connection: close.
